purpose: Registered before any trial of this experiment. The Kaggle controller refuses a config whose hashes differ and writes heldout_deviation_record.json with the Linux identity before the first held-out trial.
user_decision_2026_11_17: The user approved a new experiment: the locked primary A4 against the C++ SEM-RRT* port, both with 20 s, on Kaggle.
question: With both planners in C++ on the same hardware and the same 20 s wall-clock budget, does the locked primary A4 still meet every criterion of plan section 5.3 against SEM-RRT*?

relation_to_previous.heldout_kaggle: Spent (2026-11-16, kernel notebook66864104b1): Python SEM-RRT* with a fixed 7425 iterations; the primary passed every criterion. Never rerun, never pooled with this experiment.
relation_to_previous.sem_cpp_port: include/terrain25d/SemRrtStar.hpp, src/SemRrtStar.cpp (library sem_rrtstar_c): bit-identical to the Python reconstruction on 30/30 dev runs at 7425 iterations on Windows (logs/sem_cpp_20261117/dev_equivalence/summary.json), about 48x faster.

methods.sem_native: SEM-RRT* project reconstruction, C++ search engine (Python/scipy native raster as preprocessing), 20 s wall clock, no iteration limit.
methods.a4_rpbit_l33_m20: Locked primary (lambda 33, M = 20 convergence batches, refinement on), unchanged since the lock of 2026-11-16T03:46:05.7959372Z; 20 s cap, self-stop on convergence.

inputs.novelty: map seeds 71001-71010 and planner seeds 716001-716005 appear in no earlier config, tool, test or document

timing_protocol: Kaggle CPU session (no accelerator). execution.cores [0]: one lane, one trial at a time, so the two methods never run concurrently; the controller still requires every registered core on its own physical core.
One fresh process per trial, pinned to its lane core, one thread.
Both methods of a (map, planner seed) block run back to back on the same core; the method order alternates between blocks.

Solve clocks as registered in plan 5.3: A4 from before potential construction; SEM from planner construction, after loading the map and building the native raster and its C++ copy (reported separately as preprocessing).
gates_before_heldout: Linux build of the delivered sources; 31 CTest groups: the 30 of the previous Kaggle run plus sem_native_cpp (exact == comparisons of RNG, CPython math, libm, model edges and full solves).
smoke_fairtime: 7 smoke fixtures, 2 s, both methods; no correctness error, every A4 trial successful, strict validation.
gate_fairtime: the 5 families at map seed 51001, planner seed 516001, 20 s, both methods; same conditions.

sem_cpp_bit_identity: on the 5 gate_fairtime maps, planner seeds 516001 and 516002, Python and C++ SEM-RRT* each run 7425 iterations and must be identical in status, counters and every incumbent (10/10), on the Linux runtime of the campaign.
Any failed gate stops the run before the held-out; the cause is reported, nothing is retuned.

primary_criteria.source: plan section 5.3, unchanged; evaluated by tools/analyze_rp_bit.py criteria() for a4_rpbit_l33_m20 against sem_native
items: PSR: A4 >= SEM, pooled and in every family.
Time: A4 solve time to self-stop < SEM (20 s).
J30 = L_H + 30 E / 40 by the independent oracle: paired mean difference < 0 and its one-sided upper 95% bound < 0 (hierarchical bootstrap map -> seed, 20000 replicates, seed 61016).
APL and PRI: pooled relative difference upper 95% bound < +1% (non-inferiority); target: pooled mean difference < 0.

secondary_descriptive: Anytime table at T in {0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20} s: paired differences with the same bootstrap upper bound (equal-time comparison).
A4 time to reach the final SEM-RRT* J30 of the same slot (tolerance 0 and 1%).
SEM-RRT* iterations per run (engine speed on the Kaggle CPU).
Per-family tables and the failed attempts.
stated_expectation: At 20 s the C++ SEM-RRT* does several times the 7425 iterations of the previous held-out (on dev, Windows: 44,800-60,600 iterations and 0.42-3.0% lower native cost). The J30 margin of A4 on heldout_kaggle (-0.954 of about 154.6, about 0.6%) may shrink, vanish or reverse; STI and Time are expected to stay in favour of A4. Every outcome is reported.
rules: Started trials are never retried; no seeds are added; criteria and analysis are not changed after any held-out result is seen.
Strict per-snapshot validation of the primary method; fast independent validation of every trial.
Results are reported as measured on Kaggle Linux; their Time is not compared with Windows numbers.
limitations: Bit identity is checked up to 7425 iterations; at 20 s the C++ engine runs further on the same code.
Shared cloud VM: background load can add timing noise; both methods of a block share the core and alternate order.
SEM-RRT* is the project reconstruction, not the authors code.

supersedes.reason: r1 registered execution.cores [0, 1]; the shared lane runner (corridor_v4_execution.run_spawn_lanes) accepts only one or four lanes, found by a local Windows rehearsal of the non-held-out gates before any trial of this experiment started. r2 runs one lane on CPU 0; nothing else changes.
